title: a11y(form designer): a read-only package's field card still describes how to drag it — aria-describedby points at the drag instructions though its sensors are off
body:
**Filing gate ①: a measured defect, class (a): an accessibility description that tells a screen reader something false.** Reach: real Chromium (CDP `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`) on a dev-only harness that mounts the same `ObjectFormDesigner` the Form tab mounts, with `readOnly: true`. That is the harness class objectui#11871 and objectui#11872 were filed from. Studio's own public door (a read-only package's Form tab) was not driven. Measured by the objectui#11872 dev (report on that card, out-of-scope finding 1).

**Who acts on it:** objectui triage, grade and route. ⛔ Not a claim. Filed by the `domain:ui` execution seat 1 (`session_01DrKzdPdyLLBW3qpZ4vtk7z`).

**Serial note:** the same file as objectui#11898 (queued). Run it after that card, never alongside it.

## What happens

- A read-only package's field card "neither says nor looks draggable" (objectui#11781). Since objectui#11872, it carries no role description either.
- It still carries `aria-describedby` pointing at the drag instructions. The computed description reads "To pick up a field, press Space or Enter. While dragging, use the arrow keys to move it. …" in EN, and the ZH instructions in ZH.
- So a screen reader tells the author how to drag a card that cannot be dragged (its sensors are off).

## Where it comes from (read in source)

- dnd-kit's `useDraggable` always writes `aria-describedby` to the `DndContext`'s instructions. `useSortable`'s `attributes` argument cannot remove it.
- The card spreads `{...attributes}` (`SortableField` in `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectFormDesigner.tsx`).
- The fix needs either the card's JSX after the spread (no `aria-describedby` when `readOnly`), or the `DndContext` accessibility props (objectui#11802's surface).

## Done when

- A read-only card has no drag instructions in its accessible description, in EN and ZH.
- A writable card keeps them (the control).
- A pin per case, with a reverse check.

## Duplicate check

- Semantic issue search on objectstack-ai/objectui, *read-only form designer field card screen reader still reads drag instructions aria-describedby*: 5 hits. objectui#11872 (open, role description) and objectui#11871 (closed, keyboard drop) are the same file's other a11y cards, and neither names the description. The other 3 are unrelated components.

Dedupe words: read-only form designer card aria-describedby drag instructions · readOnly field card screen reader pick up instructions · useDraggable aria-describedby read-only
